bio.text: [Maruyama Ōkyo,] born Maruyama Masataka, was a Japanese artist active in the late 18th century. He moved to Kyoto, during which he studied artworks from Chinese, Japanese and Western sources. A personal style of Western naturalism mixed with Eastern decorative design emerged, and Ōkyo founded the Maruyama school of painting.

Okio was born in 1733. He was the son of a farmer, and as a child showed a passion for drawing. He studied the styles of all the older schools … He copied European engravings with his brush, and aspired to infuse a greater spirit of realism into the art of his own country.

source.author: Laurence Binyon
source.title: Painting in the Far East (2nd edition)

bio.text: He wandered through the mountains and learned composition and the laws of tree growth from every picturesque site. He kept about him hens and monkeys and swimming fish, and loved to sketch them in every attitude of motion.

source.author: Ernest F. Fenollosa
source.title: Epochs of Chinese and Japanese Art, Vol. II
